selectionReason: The next fifteen, in source-row order, of the 271 absent frozen rows at least one of whose KANJIDIC2 readings is used by an existing word article that declares the kanji (an automatic alignment of each word's kana against the kanji's readings), the rule announced on issue 60 after batch 136. No word article is added: 21 existing articles each gain one link to a new card. A card quizzes each reading that a declaring word article uses, unless the pinned JMdict marks the spelling as ateji or the reading as gikun; name-only readings are never quizzed; a reading type with no such reading gets an empty quizzed list. All fifteen pass, so none is set aside. The only other text change narrows the 張 card's Notes remark that said 緊 and 拡 had no kanji cards so that it names only 緊. 196 rows of the 271 group, 11 rows whose declaring articles use none of their KANJIDIC2 readings, and 644 rows with no declaring article remain.

Some titles share an English word with existing titles in a different sense (憧 "long for" and the "long" of 久 and 長; 憩 "take a break" and the "take" of 取 and others or the "break" of 壊 and 破; 懐 "become attached" and the "become" of 凝 and 成); these are not excluded from each other's quiz options.

The reading audits are the author's Python ports of the Kotlin builder; no Kotlin cross-check was run.

The scope audits do not attribute reads made through shell commands or Python, so they list cards, word articles and stroke files as unread that the reports say were read; the author checked those claims against the session events.

The issue #60 contract asks for serial reviewers with at most one active at any instant, but in both confirmation rounds the Claude and GPT confirmations overlapped in time (21:10:32-21:14:21 and 21:31:40-21:33:27 UTC), as in B137-B140; each worked only from its own packet without the other's reports.
